notes.text: Büchi acceptance: a run is accepting when it visits F infinitely often — NOT when it ends in F, because an ω-word never ends. This machine sits in "saw a" exactly after each a, so a run passes through F infinitely often precisely when the word contains infinitely many a's. In LTL that is GF a.

Type an infinite word as u(v): a finite prefix then the block that repeats forever. (a) is aaa…, ab(ba) is ab bababa…. The simulator finds a lasso — a path into a cycle that keeps revisiting F — and unrolls it twice so you can see the loop. a(b) is rejected: the single a is not infinitely many.

meta.title: Infinitely often a
meta.blurb: The canonical Büchi automaton for GF a: accepts exactly those infinite words containing infinitely many a's. Acceptance is about the cycle the run settles into, not where it stops.
